forms.exampleEnglish: When everyone is far from the food truck, Alex dials 911 on his cell phone.
forms.explanationEnglish: The when-clause supplies the time relationship in the narrated scene. Alex is third-person singular, so present-simple dial becomes dials. On his cell phone names the device used. The sentence reports this source event; it is not an imperative.
forms.explanationJapanese: when で はじまる ぶぶんは、いつの ことかを しめします。Alex は さんにんしょうの たんすうなので、げんざいの dial に s を つけて dials に します。on his cell phone は、つかった でんわを しめします。この ぶんは、ものがたりの できごとを つたえます。
